claim_label: Sufficiency of FRCP Rule 34 for algorithmic discrimination
description: This dispute centers on whether Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 34 provides adequate tools to hold AI developers and deployers accountable for algorithmic discrimination. While some believe existing discovery rules sufficiently capture deployment inputs and outputs, others argue that black-box opacity and legally shielded audits render traditional discovery ineffective.

instances.assertion: Existing civil discovery tools under Rule 34 are fully sufficient because they allow plaintiffs to request the inputs and outputs used by the deploying employer where the harm actually materializes.
Traditional civil discovery fails because companies exploit black-box opacity and shield their internal bias testing from lawsuits by having lawyers manage the audits.
